title: Nourishing Smoky Peruvian Pork Belly Tiradito
description: A Peruvian inspired dish featuring smoky pork belly slices, earthy flavors and a springy twist, perfect for a monsoon evening, this shojin friendly tiradito is a must try.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a small bowl, mix together tandoor spice mix, soy sauce, lime juice, grated ginger, and minced garlic.
Place the pork belly in a large ziplock bag and pour the marinade over it, making sure the pork is coated evenly.
Seal the bag and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Remove the pork from the marinade and place it on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Roast the pork in the preheated oven for 20 minutes or until it reaches an internal temperature of 160 degrees Fahrenheit.
Let the pork rest for 10 minutes before slicing it into thin strips.
In a small bowl, mix together chopped cilantro and sesame oil.
To assemble the tiradito, place a few slices of the pork on a plate and drizzle with the cilantro sesame oil mixture.
